stealthy

/STEL-thee/ — rhymes with healthy · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Stealthy describes an action carried out quietly and carefully so that no one else notices it.

With stealthy steps, the cat crossed the room without waking the dog.

Example

The spy moved through the building in stealthy silence, pressing against shadows and listening at each door before passing.

Stealthy captures not just quiet movement but careful, intentional action designed to avoid detection. It's not merely quiet; it's the deliberate sneakiness of trying to go unnoticed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sneaky: Sneaky is about motive: acting secretly because you are doing something you shouldn't and hope not to get caught. Stealthy is about execution — quiet, careful control of every movement. A guard on patrol can be stealthy with nothing to hide; sneaky always hints at guilt.

covert: Covert means kept deliberately secret — a covert plan or operation is hidden from outsiders as a matter of policy. Stealthy describes the doing itself: how quietly and carefully the action is carried out. A covert mission can still be executed clumsily; a stealthy one cannot.

inconspicuous: Inconspicuous means simply not attracting notice — blending in by being plain, small, or ordinary, with no effort required. Stealthy is active: someone works, step by careful step, to stay undetected. A gray coat is inconspicuous by itself; crossing a creaky floor unheard takes stealthy care.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

clumsy: moving awkwardly, noisily, without careful control

conspicuous: easily noticed, drawing everyone's attention

Where it sits · how completely unnoticed the action stays — quiet → silent → furtive → stealthy

quiet vs. stealthy: Quiet is much weaker than stealthy; quiet only describes making little sound, while stealthy adds deliberate care to stay completely undetected.

silent vs. stealthy: Silent is weaker than stealthy: silence means making no sound, but a stealthy person also controls every movement so no one even senses they are there.

furtive vs. stealthy: Furtive is slightly weaker than stealthy — a furtive person acts secretively, with darting glances that others often notice, while stealthy action is controlled so carefully that no one detects it at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — stealth

Root — stealth: secret action; originally 'theft,' from the root of 'steal' (Old English)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: characterized by (adjective-forming) (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Stealth comes from the Old English root of 'steal' — it originally meant theft itself — and -y makes it an adjective. Something stealthy is done the way a thief must move: quietly and carefully, so that no one notices.

Use the root in a new word: steal

Use the root in a new word: steal: A pickpocket can steal a wallet in a crowded subway car without breaking stride.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / informal

Use stealthy when an action is carried out quietly and carefully to avoid detection or notice. It implies deliberate, intentional concealment. For something that is naturally quiet or silent, 'quiet' or 'silent' is simpler.
